title_prompt: Start from the source in 1895. Walk into witnessed history: collect archive fragments and place truth back onto the timeline.
set_hint: Note: the game has no music or sound effects yet; these sliders will apply once audio is added.
ui_version: v0.2 Source Demo · Every person and event is sourced · Remember history, cherish peace
cw_body: This game is based on the true history of Nanjing in 1937. It contains accounts and implications of war, massacre and sexual violence — all violence is conveyed through restraint and archival form, with no graphic imagery. Every event, person and figure in this game comes from published historical sources.
cw_note: Some content may be distressing. If you are recovering from trauma, please proceed with care. May the departed rest in peace, and may the truth be remembered.
hud_date_beat0: December 11, 1937 · The Eve of the Fall
hud_torn: The patrol interrupted your recording — only a torn page remains.
hud_confiscated: The evidence was seized and destroyed.
hud_spotted: The patrol has noticed you. Take cover, and hold Shift to hold your breath.
hud_caught: You were escorted to the assembly point. Some things you cannot change — you can only decide how much you see.
obj0: Bring the fleeing family into the Ginling College refugee shelter
obj1a: Record the Ginling refugee roster in front of the main hall
obj1b: Decide what to do with the disarmed soldiers inside the gate
obj2a: Record the evidence inside the Safety Zone (6 places)
obj2b: Decide what to do at the main gate
obj2d: Meet Fitch in front of the chapel
obj3: Decide which evidence to carry out of the city (max 3)
beat0_intro: Night of December 11. The air-raid siren has rasped three times, and the city's lights go out one by one. Your name is Minnie Vautrin, dean of studies at Ginling College. Your colleagues urge you to go to Hankou; you say: I cannot leave now. The campus is becoming a shelter — first, bring that family at the gate inside.
beat1_intro: December 13. The Japanese army enters through Zhonghua Gate. Gunfire swells through the streets, then thins. Stranded Chinese soldiers lay down their arms and pour into the Safety Zone. Outside the gate, disarmed men kneel against the wall. And you must begin a new task — recording everything that is happening.
beat2_intro: December 14 to 16, night after night. Two hundred and fifty thousand people are crammed into the Safety Zone while patrols roam the streets. Soldiers push into the campus again and again. What can you do? Stand in their way. Help the wounded. And — while their backs are turned — write down every name.
beat3_intro: December 17. Fitch has decided to sew Father Magee's film into his coat and carry it out of Nanjing. He says: history needs evidence. Your bundle is small. Choose — which evidence is worth your life to carry out.
person_note_vautrin: Historical figure · Minnie Vautrin (1886–1941) · See Archive Card 03
person_note_fitch: Historical figure · George Fitch (1886–1973) · See Archive Card 01
npc_family_1: Sir… madam… please, let me and my child in. It is not safe out there anymore.
npc_family_2: Thank you. May Heaven bless you, and bless this school.
npc_family_done: We have arrived. On this whole road, you were the only one who stopped. Thank you.
npc_generic: (She looks up at you once, then lowers her head. Now is not the time for words.)
npc_r1_greet: Sir, we haven't eaten in three days… the little one cries from hunger.
npc_r1_thanks: With this food, the child can sleep tonight. Thank you, good soul.
npc_r2_greet: My leg was hit by a stray bullet — it keeps festering… is there any medicine?
npc_r2_thanks: This salve eases the pain. You saved more than my leg.
npc_r3_greet: My little sister has a fever — she talked deliriously all night… please, any medicine.
npc_r3_thanks: The fever has eased a little. When the war ends, I will bow to you.
npc_r4_greet: The nights are so cold… the old man's cough grows worse.
npc_r4_thanks: Tonight I can sleep through. A house of kindness shall have its reward.
npc_r5_greet: Mother lies sick in bed; the blanket cannot cover her through the night…
npc_r5_thanks: Mother says: thank the teacher of the foreign school. We will remember you.
npc_r6_greet: Our family of seven scattered — three are missing… I have not eaten for two days.
npc_r6_thanks: When I find my children, I will tell them: this is the one who saved me.
c1_title: Inside the main gate, disarmed Chinese soldiers kneel against the wall. Under the Japanese army's orders, sheltering stragglers could doom the entire shelter.
c1_a: Let them in, and give them civilian clothes
c1_b: Point them toward the refugee camp and close the gate
c1_ra: You buried their uniforms in the back garden. The diary will record this: that day, the Safety Zone gained one more keeper of a quiet conscience.
c1_rb: They bowed to the ground and vanished into the alley. Years later you will still remember the eyes beneath that wall — you did not open the door.
c2_title: At the campus gate, patrolmen are dragging away three women in hiding. You are only steps away — you can step in front of them, or withdraw and record what is happening.
c2_a: Step forward, and stand in front of the women
c2_b: Withdraw inside, and write this scene into the diary
c2_ra: You stood in the doorway. The soldiers stared for a long time at the American armband, then swore and left. You brought the three women into the main hall — but the patrol has remembered your face. (Patrols grow more alert from now on.)
c2_rb: You withdrew inside and wrote down the time, the numbers and the faces with trembling fingers. Those three pages of the diary later became evidence at the trials. (The three women were taken away.)
dlg_leave: There is nothing I can spare right now…
dlg_give_confirm: Once given, it cannot be taken back. Are you sure?
fitch_1: Minnie, I have sewn Magee's film into the lining of my coat. We leave the city at first light. Those pages you have gathered — the bundle is small; it holds only three. Choose what history keeps.
fitch_choice_stay: Wait — let me look once more
walk_line1: On the road out of the city, no one speaks.
walk_line2: The bundle presses against your back like a cold stone monument.
walk_line3: The walls fall behind you, and the gunfire fades.
walk_line4: What you carry out is not paper — it is what you will one day say to the world.
montage_1: 1938. Magee's film is screened in America. The atrocities in Nanjing are confirmed by moving images for the first time.
montage_2: 1946–1948. The Tokyo and Nanjing trials open. Diaries, film and rosters become exhibits before the courts.
montage_3: Iwane Matsui — hanged, December 23, 1948. Yasuji Okamura's peer Hisao Tani — executed by firing squad in Nanjing, 1947.
montage_4: And the names that city lost remain forever in the winter of 1937.
set_what_left: Today's history is what someone once risked their life to choose.
gal_title: Archive Gallery · Your Museum of Memory
card1_quote: The 16mm reel turns in the projector; on the screen, a burning city and carts carrying the dead.
card1_source: Film footage by Rev. John Magee (1937–38), later evidence at the Tokyo Trial.
card1_note: Sewn into Fitch's coat and carried out of Nanjing — among humanity's earliest filmed records of atrocity.
card2_quote: This is not a war film. This is real Nanjing.
card2_source: The Diaries of John Rabe (daily entries 1937–38, published 1997).
card2_note: John Rabe, chairman of the International Committee for the Safety Zone, recorded the Zone's daily life and the army's atrocities.
card3_quote: Night of December 16: I dare not keep the lamp lit… I do not know how many I can still shelter tomorrow.
card3_source: The Diaries of Minnie Vautrin (1937–40, published 2000).
card3_note: Minnie Vautrin, dean of Ginling College, kept a daily record of the Ginling refugee shelter.
card4_quote: Every name is proof that someone existed.
card4_source: Registration ledger of the Ginling College refugee shelter (Dec 1937).
card4_note: The ledger recorded each sheltered woman's name, age and place of origin.
card5_quote: Three slash wounds on the back; one gunshot wound on the right shoulder…
card5_source: Medical records of Gulou (University) Hospital, kept by Dr. Robert Wilson.
card5_note: Wilson was the only surgeon who stayed on duty after the city fell.
card6_quote: We respectfully submit to Your Embassy the report of this case, No. X…
card6_source: Protest documents from the International Committee to the Japanese Embassy (from Dec 1937).
card6_note: The Committee recorded atrocities and filed protests almost daily — these documents later underpinned the trials.
card7_quote: Hundred-man killing contest beyond record: Mukai 106 — Noda 105, both lieutenants extend the match
card7_source: Continuous reports in the Tokyo Nichi Nichi Shimbun, Nov–Dec 1937.
card7_note: The perpetrators' own press became evidence. Mukai Toshiaki and Noda Tsuyoshi were executed in Nanjing on January 28, 1948.
card8_quote: Over 200,000 — the International Military Tribunal for the Far East (1948); over 300,000 — the Nanjing War Crimes Tribunal (1947); the Memorial Hall recognizes 300,000+.
card8_source: IMTFE judgment; Nanjing War Crimes Tribunal verdict; the Nanjing Massacre Memorial Hall.
card8_note: The figures are not vague — they are the rulings of different courts. This is how to read historical numbers.
card9_quote: Matsui hanged (1948); Tani shot (1947); Prince Asaka spared prosecution by imperial status.
card9_source: Verdicts of the Tokyo and Nanjing trials.
card9_note: Imperial immunity remains debated among historians — presenting the debate is itself history education.
card10_quote_high: In that school, someone stood in front of us at the gate, someone shared their last handful of rice. We told it again and again, until the world listened.
card10_quote_mid: The survivors spoke it aloud. As long as one person remembers, it has not truly vanished.
card10_quote_none: Nothing could be carried out. But the one who saw is still alive — where memory lives, witnessing lives.
card10_source: Collections of survivor testimony (archives and memorial halls worldwide).
card10_note: This card is generated by your own witnessing — every playthrough differs, as history is made of countless eyes.
tut_move: A/D to move · S to crouch and hold your breath (slower, less likely to be noticed) · E to interact and vault
tut_record: Walk to a glowing page and hold E for about 1.2 seconds to record. Being seen interrupts you.
tut_sneak: The red cone is the patrol's field of view. Crouch (S) to stay low, or push crates for a boost, throw stones to distract, and slip through steam cover.

hub_subtitle: Begin at the source. Light up history, one witnessed chapter at a time.
hub_hint: Click a year node or use arrow keys, then press Enter to enter.
hub_desc_source: 1895–1910 · How Taiwan and the Korean Peninsula were drawn in — it all starts here.
hub_desc_1931: 1931 · Gunfire in Mukden; the three northeastern provinces fall (in development).
hub_desc_1937: 1937 · In December Nanjing falls. In the Safety Zone, someone begins to record.
hub_desc_1942: 1942 · The war reaches Malaya — Parit Sulong and Sandakan (in development).
hub_desc_1948: 1946–48 · The tribunals in Tokyo and Nanjing — the reckoning of history (in development).
pro_intro: In the archive workshop an empty map of East Asia lies on the table. To bear witness, start at the source — history did not begin in 1937. Six archive fragments are scattered across the room. Find them all.
pro_prompt_pickup: Press E to pick up the fragment
pro_prompt_board: Press E to open the timeline board
pro_all_collected: All fragments found. Put them back on the timeline.
pro_obj_board: Go to the long table and place the fragments on the timeline board
pro_obj_witness: Witness the memories as they light up
tut2_move: A/D to move · Press E at a table edge or step to vault
tut2_move_pickup: Walk near a glowing paper and press E to pick it up
tut2_board: You have every fragment. Go to the timeline board on the right wall and press E to open it.
pro_board_title: Timeline Board · Return each document to its year
pro_board_hint: ◀ ▶ choose a fragment, then choose its year. Wrong answers cost nothing — just read it again.
pro_board_correct: Correct. A corner of history returns to its place.
pro_board_wrong: This page does not belong to that year. Read it again.
pro_frag_1895c: Newspaper clipping · The disposal of the Formosans
pro_scene1895_1: The Treaty of Shimonoseki is signed. Article 2: China cedes to Japan in perpetuity the island of Taiwan together with all adjacent islands and the Pescadores…
pro_scene1895_2: Taiwan thus enters fifty years of Japanese colonial rule. Colonisation begins as ink on paper — then lands on the doorplate of every household.
pro_scene1910_1: The Japan–Korea Annexation Treaty takes effect. The Emperor of Korea makes a complete and permanent cession of all rights of sovereignty over Korea to the Emperor of Japan.
pro_scene1910_2: The peninsula enters thirty-five years of colonial rule. Names, languages and land begin to be numbered by another set of rules.
pro_outro_1: A little more light on the wall map. After the source come the guns of Mukden in 1931 — and further south, Nanjing in the winter of 1937.
pro_outro_2: The archive is not closed — next chapter: 1931 · Mukden Incident (in development). History still has a long road ahead.
card11_quote: China cedes to Japan in perpetuity… the island of Taiwan with all adjacent islands, and the Pescadores.
card11_source: Treaty of Shimonoseki, Article 2 (signed 17 April 1895) — public treaty document.
card11_note: This treaty put Taiwan and the Pescadores under fifty years of Japanese rule. Colonial rule is where all these stories begin.
card12_quote: The Emperor of Korea makes a complete and permanent cession of all rights of sovereignty over Korea to the Emperor of Japan.
card12_source: Japan–Korea Annexation Treaty (effective 29 August 1910) — public treaty document.
card12_note: The Korean Peninsula entered thirty-five years of colonial rule. Resistance and witness began the day it was signed.
